title: Scoped obstruction: helper468 must end at rank eight after B88's target MOVE
body:
## Result and scope

**Scoped negative result / exact boundary certificate. No new circuit, supplier or kappa.**

For helper **468** in the fixed PR589 R439 bit word, the first rank-eight two-sided boundary footprint occurs at **cut 177**, when zero-based **B gate 88 moves target 208 from frame 0 to frame 152**, before its ADD. Applying Ali Romman's PR1128 boundary lemma, **any permitted reversible linear suffix starting there or later must end helper 468 at rank eight**. The class allows arbitrary rational frames, arbitrary suffix length, target access and extra restored dirty auxiliaries, with common-frame scalar operations and monotone frame changes; it excludes new COPY/descent/reset or altered prefixes.

All **4,697 later cuts** have that general rank-eight obstruction. The earlier 177 cuts pass the two-sided rank-seven test and are not existence certificates. At those earlier cuts, an arbitrary **one-common-frame restore-and-isolate block** of rank at most seven is separately excluded because it would promote target 208 into an incompatible frame.

The complete ledger covers **4,874 boundaries**, including the initial post-scatter cut and every **1,310 MOVE / 3,563 individual ADD** boundary through original B/C and final MOVEs. Two different engines agree on every event, cut, restoration/dirty mask, geometry case and all 661 final forward/inverse columns.

| Exclusion | Cuts |
|---|---:|
| Rank-seven footprint forces target 208 into an incompatible frame |177|
| Footprint already spans rank eight |1557|
| Helper468 already has rank eight |3140|

Nine explicit frame-join certificates use nonzero integer minors and exact annihilating/separating normals. At the critical MOVE the scalar restoration row and dirty column remain unchanged, while the join's rank grows 7→8; its eight-line determinant is -32.

## Task, predecessor credit and delta

Fresh OS seed **17**, bit supplier track. Exact base `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`. [Claim/discussion1362](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1362).

[PR1256](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1256), pinned at `d6d5a994fcdcd8d04ec439ff988daa8f37b17ece`, supplies the initial-cut fixture and explicitly leaves later target-read cuts open. [PR1128](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1128), pinned at `df29b159239b79d7e451d6ddda826a73e0e50a67`, owns the general two-sided restoration/erasure lemma and its two earlier boundary analyses. **The new result is its complete later-cut application and the exact B88 transition, not a new general lemma.** Its earlier exploratory single-register readout scan did not supply this whole-cut restore/isolate theorem or earlier general-suffix cutoff.

This changes the card from the already covered H2/K repair (PR1194/1311) to a residual/H4 boundary audit. It retains the assigned bit track. PR1253's fixed first-contact kernel entrances are a different question. Refreshed overlap covered 861 open PR bodies and 108 discussion/comment records, plus 60 recent all-state PRs; dependency heads were rechecked before submission. Coverage limits are recorded.

Only `research/r439-helper 468-late-cut/` is added. The first 177 cuts remain open for staged mechanisms; new transport or a changed earlier prefix is outside the theorem. Any staged attempt keeping the original prefix must start before the target 208 MOVE. No selected frontier or frozen source is changed.

## Accounting and validation

The README/proof gives a favorable ideal two-slot width-seven invoice: retain all nine COPY/ERASE pairs, return all eight freed old host coordinates, consume an idle rank-seven slot, and account for the changed helper path. Both ideal deltas preserve rank mass and lower child count/moment. Preparation, source/storage, restoration and frame overhead are optimistically free in that screen. It is not an implemented invoice or physical host assignment; the boundary failures remain even under free added work.

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/r439-helper 468-late-cut/verify.py
```

Expected:

```text
PASS_R439_HELPER468_LATE_CUT cuts=4874 excluded=4874 joins=9 arbitrary_suffix_from=177 new_kappa=false
```

Independent replay:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/r439-helper 468-late-cut/independent.py
```

Full registered replay passes on Python 3.12.15:

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/r439-helper 468-late-cut
```

All **ten tests** pass on Python 3.12.15 and 3.14.7. Mathematical regressions cover 168 invertible binary 3×3 matrices, 1008 inverse updates and 10080 outside-frame span cases. Controls reject archive drift, omitted cuts/MOVEs, false minors/normals and receipt overwrites. Both engines pass under `-I -O -S -B` after isolated relocation without writing files. Four source archives match exact Git blobs. The card's original R439 working example also passes.

No native, new hosted/precision invoice, selected cold replay, remote CI pass or full multiplication formalization is claimed. Finite regressions check implementations; the written necessary-condition proof supplies the unbounded suffix/block scope.

## Credit and next question

Credit **Ross Richardson/PR1256**, **Ali Romman/PR1128 and PR1043**, **DreamingOfClouds/PR589**, **eumemic/PR555/543**, **Sagar Thakrar/PR1023**, and the retained contributors in the unchanged NOTICE. Exact commits, Git blobs and archive hashes are in SOURCES.json; Apache-2.0 licensing is retained.

New work by **Cinna Davis (@1337isnot1337)** with substantial **OpenAI Codex assistance**. Both engines belong to this contribution; independent human review is not claimed.

Next step: one priced staged mechanism before the critical MOVE, with a full dirty-column replay, legal changed continuation and complete source/frame/restoration/hosting charges. The proof does not establish its existence.
